questions.question: Biology is derived from which Greek words?
questions.explanation: Bios means life and logos means study.

questions.question: Biology is best defined as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Biology is the science of life and living organisms.

questions.question: Anatomy is the study of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Anatomy deals with the structures of organisms.

questions.question: Biochemistry focuses on which of the following?
questions.explanation: Biochemistry studies chemical reactions required for life.

questions.question: Bioinformatics uses information technology for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bioinformatics handles genomic and biological data using information technology.

questions.question: Biotechnology involves the manipulation of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Biotechnology manipulates living matter including genetic modification.

questions.question: Ecology studies interactions of organisms with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ecology studies interactions between organisms and their environment.

questions.question: Genetics is the study of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Genetics focuses on genes and heredity.

questions.question: Physiology is the study of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Physiology studies functions and mechanisms in living organisms.

questions.question: Microbiology is the study of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Microbiology studies microscopic organisms and their interactions.

questions.question: Living things include plants animals and which other group?
questions.explanation: Living things include plants animals and microorganisms.

questions.question: Living things were initially classified into which two groups?
questions.explanation: Early classification placed living things as plants or animals.

questions.question: Both plants and animals have which cell type?
questions.explanation: Plants and animals are both eukaryotic organisms.

questions.question: Animals are generally described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Animals are motile and heterotrophic organisms.

questions.question: Bacteria are neither plants nor animals because they are which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes and lack a nucleus.

questions.question: Classification of living things includes how many levels?
questions.explanation: The levels are kingdom phylum class order family genus and species.

questions.question: The most fundamental classification of living things is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the most fundamental classification level.

questions.question: The current number of kingdoms is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The five kingdoms are Animalia Plantae Monera Protista and Fungi.

questions.question: Placement into kingdoms is based on food acquisition cell type and which other factor?
questions.explanation: Kingdoms are based on food acquisition cell type and cell number.

questions.question: Phylum follows which classification level?
questions.explanation: Phylum comes after kingdom in the classification hierarchy.

questions.question: Phylum seeks physical resemblance that suggests which of the following?
questions.explanation: Physical similarities in a phylum suggest common ancestry.

questions.question: Classes further subdivide which classification level?
questions.explanation: Classes are subdivisions of a phylum.

questions.question: Humans belong to the mammal class because they do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mammals are named for drinking milk as babies.

questions.question: Orders are further broken down from which classification level?
questions.explanation: Orders are subdivisions of classes.

questions.question: A taxonomy key is best described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: A taxonomy key is a checklist of characteristics used for grouping.

questions.question: Orders are divided into which classification level?
questions.explanation: Families are the classification level below order.

questions.question: Organisms within a family are said to be related because of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Family members are considered related because of familiarity.

questions.question: Genus completes which part of the two-part name?
questions.explanation: The genus forms the first part of an organism's two-part name.

questions.question: Genus classification is very specific so it contains which of the following?
questions.explanation: A genus is specific and contains fewer organisms than higher levels.

questions.question: Species is which classification level?
questions.explanation: Species is the lowest and most exacting classification level.

questions.question: The main pattern for species placement is the ability to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: Organisms of the same species can breed with one another.

questions.question: Animalia cell wall is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Animalia cells lack a cell wall.

questions.question: Plantae mode of nutrition is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Plantae are autotrophic organisms.

questions.question: Monera nuclear membrane is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Monera are prokaryotes and lack a nuclear membrane.

questions.question: Protista is described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Protista are unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

questions.question: Fungi cannot make their own food because they are which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic and cannot make their own food.

questions.question: Monera cell wall is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Monera have a noncellulosic cell wall.

questions.question: Animalia organization level includes which of the following?
questions.explanation: Animalia show tissue organ or organ system organization.

questions.question: Organisms are classified by source of energy and source of which element?
questions.explanation: Classification considers energy source and carbon source.

questions.question: Autotrophs use inorganic sources while heterotrophs consume which of the following?
questions.explanation: Heterotrophs obtain energy by consuming organic matter.

questions.question: Autotrophs produce energy-rich organic compounds using which sources?
questions.explanation: Autotrophs use inorganic sources to make organic compounds.

questions.question: Autotroph examples include plants algae and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Some bacteria are autotrophic along with plants and algae.

questions.question: Heterotrophs obtain energy by consuming which of the following?
questions.explanation: Heterotrophs rely on organic matter for energy.

questions.question: Heterotroph examples include animals fungi and which of the following?
questions.explanation: Most bacteria are heterotrophic along with animals and fungi.

questions.question: Autotrophs are divided into photoautotrophs and which other type?
questions.explanation: The two autotroph types are photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs.

questions.question: Photoautotrophs use which energy source?
questions.explanation: Photoautotrophs use sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Chemoautotrophs use energy from which of the following?
questions.explanation: Chemoautotrophs use energy from chemical reactions.

questions.question: Heterotrophs are divided into photoheterotrophs and which other type?
questions.explanation: The two heterotroph types are photoheterotrophs and chemoheterotrophs.

questions.question: Photoheterotrophs obtain energy from sunlight and carbon from which of the following?
questions.explanation: Photoheterotrophs use sunlight for energy but organic matter for carbon.

questions.question: Chemoheterotrophs obtain energy by consuming which of the following?
questions.explanation: Chemoheterotrophs consume organic compounds produced by other organisms.
